fichas.title: Railway station layouts
fichas.summary: Stations are classified by track arrangement and the location of the station building. The page illustrates eight arrangements, including through stations, termini, multi-level and island stations, and different passenger access configurations.

fichas.title: Station planning and design basics
fichas.summary: Station design priorities include operational safety, passenger security and well-being, easy orientation, maintainability, brand recognition, and attractive form. Stations should provide short walking routes to other transport, with local public transport near platforms and provision for parking and vehicle drop-off. Station buildings may include railway services, waiting areas, shops, and luggage storage. The approach line and station arrangement should suit the urban context; the text identifies a low-level arrangement as the most acceptable urban-planning variant.

fichas.title: Pedestrian underpasses and bridges
fichas.summary: The text gives minimum widths and clearance heights for pedestrian underpasses and bridges. It recommends that larger widths be set as multiples of the stated walking width and notes a reduced minimum clearance beneath supplementary installations.
uses: Pedestrian circulation between platforms or across railway tracks

fichas.title: Station accessibility
fichas.summary: Stations where more than the stated daily passenger threshold catch trains should provide at least one barrier-free access. Ramps are described as maintenance-free; lifts should be pass-through and glazed. Access to platforms is permitted only along the platform, with a waiting area in front of the lift. Tactile and colour-contrasted guide strips, hazard markings, and Braille platform numbering are also recommended.
uses: Passenger movement with prams, pushchairs, luggage trolleys, and cycles

dimensions.context: If more than this number of passengers per day catch a train, provide at least one barrier-free access
dimensions.ocr_raw: If more than 1000 passengers per day catch a train, then at least one barrier-free access ... should be provided.
